name: MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B

lineage.how_derived: supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-9B on MiMo-generated data (77.4B tokens total, 27.2B loss-bearing): code 29.9 %, cyber 14.2 %, general 28.5 %, visual 27.4 % of tokens (card table). The card calls the checkpoint the SFT stage; an RL follow-up of this distill is requested in discussion 2 but not released.

purpose: The card states: a 9B agentic model developed by Xiaomi MiMo through supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-9B on MiMo-generated data, covering coding, general-purpose agent tasks, visual coding and cybersecurity, released as the SFT checkpoint and a starting point for open research in agentic reinforcement learning.

license.name: MIT (card tag)
license.notes: Card YAML says license mit; no LICENSE file in the repository (404 on raw/main/LICENSE, 2026-11-19), so no licence text was read. The card also carries a 'Use Restrictions' notice (no unlawful use, no military use, no malicious cyber activity, no autonomous high-risk actions without human oversight, among others) that it says is informational only and does not amend the licence. Base Qwen3.5-9B is Apache-2.0 per the qwen3.5-9b record.

architecture.kind: dense hybrid Gated DeltaNet + gated attention (Qwen3.5-9B architecture, model_type qwen3_5) with vision tower
architecture.attention: full attention every 4th layer (full_attention_interval 4, so 8 full-attention and 24 linear-attention layers), 16 Q / 4 KV heads, head dim 256, hidden 4096, FFN 12288
architecture.drafter: none shipped: config.json declares mtp_num_hidden_layers 1 but the safetensors index has no mtp tensors (0 matches, 2026-11-19); community adds the Qwen3.5-9B MTP head separately (discussion 8)
architecture.why_this_design: Unchanged from Qwen3.5-9B; the card describes only the SFT data mixture and the role as an RL starting point, with no architecture reasons.

strengths: Vendor SWE-bench Pro gain over the base (32.0 to 44.6) and large agent-task gains (AutomationBench 5.0 to 30.3, Terminal-Bench 2.1 27.0 to 37.1) for a 9B
Fits 12 to 16 GB cards at Q6_K to Q8_0; very popular GGUF (about 950k downloads for the bartowski repo)
Long context works with YaRN (user: 40/40 needles at 512K, no short-task loss)
On GSM8K a user measured the same accuracy as the base with 150 to 400 think tokens instead of 1800 to 3500
weaknesses: SWE-bench Verified gain over Qwen3.5-9B is small (61.1 vs 60.0, vendor), and a commenter mocked the avg@3 reporting (discussion 10)
Thinking chains can still run long on hard questions: at temperature 0 an 8K cap truncated over half of GPQA attempts (user report, discussion 13)
llama.cpp template needs a community fix for tool calls; reasoning boundary can leak </think> into content
Many vendor scores are on internal MiMo evaluation sets
Tool-calling loops are reported (discussion 16, unreviewed weight-editing experiment, no statistics yet)
soft.behavior: Thinking via enable_thinking. generation_config.json sets temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95; llama-cli defaults min_p 0.05 while Ollama defaults to 0, a commenter suggests min_p 0 or 0.03 (discussion 12). The user comparison in discussion 15 found much shorter think chains than the base on GSM8K, while discussion 13 found long chains on GPQA: length depends on the task. Budget generous max tokens for reasoning.
best_for: agentic coding and tool use on 12 to 16 GB GPUs
avoid_for: hard reasoning under short token budgets

user_reports.summary: Stock llama.cpp template picks the wrong parser: reasoning_content empty and tool calls unreliable; a community template fixes both (confirmed on an RTX 3090)
Upstream template on a BF16 GGUF can emit a literal </think> inside content with an empty reasoning_content on some prompts, reproduced at temperature 0
YaRN x2 to 512K works on Q8_0 with an RX 7900 XTX: 40/40 needles, 74 tok/s decode; thinking chains long

474-run audit on an RTX 5080 laptop: 96/100 on GSM8K like the base Qwen3.5-9B but 5 s per question instead of 61 s (12x faster) because the think chain is 150 to 400 tokens; author concludes it is not smarter in math, only more efficient (own harness, single author)

Adding the Qwen3.5-9B MTP head to a Q8_0 GGUF raised decode from about 93 tok/s overall to 123 to 165 tok/s depending on category (coding 165) with acceptance 0.43 to 0.75 (poster says about +50 percent); another user objects that the head was not trained for this distill and acceptance may fall

soft.maturity: Xiaomi MiMo is an established lab with the MiMo-V2.6 family (Flash and Pro, see mimo-v2.6-flash-mopd); heavy community uptake (about 31k downloads and 713 likes on the base repo, 16 discussion threads, many quant and ablation derivatives).

tona_fit.reason: An MIT-tagged 9B agent model on the Qwen3.5 architecture that fits the 12 and 16 GB classes with good agent numbers (vendor) and short think chains on easy tasks (user), complementing the A3B MoEs for users with little RAM. Needs an own agent and Rust/Go evaluation against Qwen3.5-9B, since the SWE-bench Verified gain is small and most vendor scores are on internal or non-independent sets.
blockers: dense Qwen3.5-9B path in Tona not confirmed
